text:
emma: Heads-up — brought up comet24k-int4 on a staging GPU pool and seeing weird KV shadowing after ~18k tokens. Not a simple off-by-one; outputs start drifting vs float baseline. Repro steps below.

raj: ugh. can you paste the run command and the exact prompt used?

emma: sure — running on ded-1 with the quant build. command: `rwi-bench --model comet24k-int4 --ctx 32768 --seed 42 --profile kv,rope --prompt-file tests/long_anchor.txt`

oliver: what's the test prompt look like?

emma: short excerpt: `A: <anchor-token repeated 512x> B: subsequent natural language passage...` trying to simulate a long anchored prefix followed by a long continuation.

raj: interesting. does float32 comet24k on the same harness diverge?

emma: float32 baseline holds for the full 32k and matches expected logits. int4 starts diverging around token 18000 onwards — pattern looks like a shadow copy of an earlier segment, like the KV indices shifted by a fixed offset.

sasha: can you share a tiny diff of outputs (float vs int4) for a failing window? a few tokens will do.

emma: pasted below (first mismatch snippet):
```
# position 17998..18002
float: " the server responded with a 200 OK and returned the expected payload."
int4:  " the server responded with a 200 OK and returned the expected payload.the server responded with"
```

raj: that looks like a repeated sequence appended — smells like KV index wrap or RoPE phase misalignment after the quant mempack. possible causes: quantized KV packing uses a different stride or an int4 kernel has a fencepost bug.

oliver: did you try forcing the rotary scaling constant back to the baseline? (we changed posscale heuristics for int4 bringup).

emma: yes — forced posscale to 1.0 and still repros, latency changed slightly.

bench-bot: automated run summary — comet24k-int4 @ded-1, ctx=32768, run_id=2026-03-23-01, mismatch_start_token=17996, mismatch_rate=0.0021, avg_latency=42ms/token (quant path), baseline_float avg_latency=128ms/token. Full logs at https://internal.redwood/comet24k/2026-03-23-01

raj: thanks. can you dump the raw KV indices around the boundary (hex) for both runs? if the index computation changed we should see shifted keys.

emma: grabbing now. small dump: `kv_index[pos=17990..18005] float= [0x1a3,0x1a4,...] int4= [0x1a3,0x1a4,...,0x1a3]` — you can see an extra repeat of an earlier block in the int4 dump.

oliver: hm. could be a prefetch/deferred write that doesn't respect atomic stride when packing int4 into 32-bit lanes. I remember a similar symptom in shard-join tests but not exactly this.

sasha: any chance it's tokenizer alignment? the int4 path uses concatenated priming where we precompute offsets. Tokenization mismatch would usually fail earlier though.

emma: tokenizer identical. verified checksums of token ids for both runs.

raj: next steps I propose: 1) run with kv_debug=1 to log per-layer KV write offsets, 2) try int8 to see if the problem is specific to the int4 packing path, 3) reproduce on a different GPU family to rule out kernel-level races.

emma: kicking that off now: `rwi-bench --model comet24k-int4 --ctx 32768 --kv_debug=1 --profile kv`

infra-bot: scheduled job ded-2:comet24k-int8-test (jid=87421) started on ded-2; notifying channel when complete.

bench-bot: quick int8 smoke (ded-2) completed — int8 shows no shadowing in first 50k tokens, mismatch_rate=0.00003 vs float baseline.

raj: int8 clean is a strong hint that the int4 packing path is the culprit. can you repro deterministically with a simple synthetic loop (repeated anchor tokens) to isolate whether it's data-dependent?

emma: synthetic loop run attached: `for i in 0..20000: append(anchor) generate(1)` — repro still triggers after ~18k tokens. deterministic across seeds.

oliver: good. let's open a kernel bug ticket and include KV dump, hex indices, and module: `quant_pack_int4.cu` — tag `@infra` and `@hw-kernels` for visibility. also add a test in the long-context CI with a repeated-anchor to catch regressions.

sasha: I'll draft the canary and add a gating eval in the nightly postquant pipeline. suggestion: run synthetic loop on int4 for at least 40k tokens and assert no repeats.

emma: created ticket RED-ML-4821 with logs and dump. link: https://redwood.atlassian/RED-ML-4821

raj: one more hypothesis — RoPE interpolation code for the quant path applies a simplified angle table with lower precision and may underflow at very high positions, causing repeated phase patterns. try enabling the full double-precision RoPE table in the quant path and rerun.

emma: toggled `rope_table_precision=double` and launching.

bench-bot: rope double run finished — int4 w/ double-precision RoPE: mismatch still occurs but shifted to token ~21000. suggests RoPE precision interacts but is not the sole cause.

oliver: thanks for the systematic checks. given int8 clean, int4 broken, and rope precision shifts timing, likely a combined effect: (a) packing stride bug causing KV miswrite, (b) precision-induced phase aliasing accelerating the visible symptom. fix plan: 1) patch quant_pack to respect atomic stride and write ordering, 2) add a defensive fence after KV writes on the quant path, 3) add a long-anchor synthetic CI.

sasha: I'll own adding the CI test and the nightly alert.

emma: good — I'll prototype the quant_pack fix and run a full 50k token stress on ded-3. will post PR link when ready. thanks team :thumbsup:

raj: ping @oliver when you have the PR; we'll coordinate kernel review.

emma: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rwi-runtime/pull/5891 — includes unit tests and the reproducer harness. will land after kernel signoff.

infra-bot: ded-3 stress job started (jid=87458). estimated run 3h.

oliver: great work — this one was subtle. keep monitoring other models on int4.

emma: will follow up with a short postmortem if/when we fix. thanks all!
